hypothesis: Train holds 150 prompts x 18 models with each model exactly once per prompt. If the hidden test shares this structure, recovering prompt groups from text and assigning models one-to-one within each group improves balanced accuracy over independent argmax.
base_scores: Unchanged v7 evidence (StyleDistance C=64 half blend with v4); no refit, no new classifier.

assignment.clustering: average-linkage cosine agglomerative, n_clusters=round(rows/18), recursively split clusters above 18
assignment.matching: scipy linear_sum_assignment on -log softmax(evidence) per recovered group

selection_history: Idea taken from public Kaggle notebooks using within-prompt Hungarian matching (e.g. sangam21/two-stage-lora-gaussian-full-hungarian-0-604), read 2026-10-22.
Probe scripts/probe_assignment_v8.py compared uncapped vs capped clustering and Sinkhorn on v7 development OOF; capped clustering chosen there (0.5071 vs 0.5249). Sinkhorn rejected (no gain).
Related-prompt split was evaluated once with the chosen recipe after selection.
limitations: Gain depends entirely on the hidden test containing complete or near-complete prompt groups; that is inferred from train and public notebooks, not verified.
Predictions are transductive: a test passage's label depends on other test passages.
Both validation partitions reuse inspected labels; the selection was adaptive.
